How to play

How to play — 3 steps
  1. Pick a colony in the Play tab — tap a tile to read what it does, then hit START.
  2. Play cards from your hand with Food 🍯. Units go to your front line (max 4); tap a ready ant, then tap a target.
  3. Bring the enemy Queen to 0 HP. Lose yours, lose the colony. The full rules are just below.
How to play — 30 seconds
  1. Goal: bring the enemy Queen to 0 HP. Lose yours, lose the colony.
  2. Food 🍯 pays for cards. Your food cap grows +1 each turn and refills every turn.
  3. ⚖️ First-turn balance: You move first, so Veritas — going second — starts with 5 cards instead of 4 and gets +1 Food on its first turn only. Going first sets the tempo; this is the standard compensation so it isn't a free advantage.
  4. Play a card: tap any card in your hand you can afford. Units go to your front line (max 4).
  5. Misclick? Hit ↩ Undo to take back the last card you played — it returns to your hand and its Food is refunded, effects and all. Only the most recent card, and only before you attack or end your turn.
  6. Bad opening hand? Hit 🔄 Redraw hand before your first play — your four cards go back in the deck and you draw a fresh hand. Once per game.
  7. 🏛️ Colony action: every colony gets one signature button in the turn controls — usable once per turn, paid in Food, and ↩ Undo takes it back just like a card. Veritas has one too — watch the Battle Log for it. Each colony's action:
  8. 🍃 Leafcutters — Tend the Garden (1🍯): heal your Queen for 2, or heal one of your ants for 2.
  9. 🌿 Canopy — Goo Spray (1🍯): one enemy ant gets −1 Attack, permanently.
  10. 🔥 Army Ants — Swarm Call (2🍯): summon a 1/1 Swarm Raider with Rush ⚡ — only if your front line has room.
  11. 💥 Exploding Ants — Prime the Glands (1🍯): one of your ants gets +1 Attack until end of turn. Veritas primes its strongest ready martyr before it attacks.
  12. 🕸️ Silk Weavers — Stitch (1🍯): one of your ants gets +1 Health, permanently.
  13. 🍯 Living Reservoirs — Nourish (2🍯): heal your Queen for 3, or heal one of your Guard ants for 3.
  14. 🍄 Zombie Ants — Spore Drift (1🍯): if an enemy ant is already infected, one more random enemy ant catches the spores. It can't start an infection from nothing.
  15. ⚡ Trap-Jaw Ants — Snap (1🍯): deal 1 damage to an enemy ant.
  16. ⭐ Special Skill (ultimate): every colony also has one big move — free, once per match. Its button sits in the turn controls next to the colony action; once fired it's spent for the whole game, and ↩ Undo takes it back just like a card. Veritas has one too — watch the Battle Log for Grand Detonation. Each colony's ultimate:
  17. 🍃 Leafcutters — Fungus Bloom: heal your Queen for 8 and gain 3 Food this turn.
  18. 🌿 Canopy — Goo Storm: all enemy ants get −2 Attack, permanently.
  19. 🔥 Army Ants — War Drums: all your ants gain +2 Attack until end of turn.
  20. 💥 Exploding Ants — Grand Detonation: deal 2 damage to all enemy ants and the enemy Queen.
  21. 🕸️ Silk Weavers — The Great Weave: all your ants gain +2 Health, permanently.
  22. 🍯 Living Reservoirs — The Ancient Replete: summon a 5/6 Guard ant — only if your front line has room; with a full line the button stays off and nothing is spent.
  23. 🍄 Zombie Ants — Spore Plague: infect all enemy ants.
  24. ⚡ Trap-Jaw Ants — The Perfect Snap: deal 2 damage to all enemy ants — or 2 damage to the enemy Queen if the front line is empty.
  25. Attack: tap one of your ready ants (gold glow), then tap an enemy ant — or the enemy Queen herself.
  26. Guard 🛡️ units must be killed first — you can't reach the Queen or other ants while a Guard stands.
  27. First-Strike ⚡ (Trap-Jaw Ants): a First-Strike ant deals its damage first — if the snap kills the enemy ant, the enemy never hits back. It does nothing against the Queen, and Guards still block as normal.
  28. New ants are tired and can't attack the turn they're played — unless they have Rush ⚡. Defenders bite back when attacked; the Queen doesn't.
  29. Done? Hit End Turn and Veritas plays. Watch the Battle Log to see my moves.
  30. 🌿 Canopy extras: 💥 Exploding ants burst when they die — killing one can kill the killer. Sticky goo permanently lowers an enemy ant's Attack. Goo Burst and Nest Seal need a target: tap the spell, then tap the ant. A living Door-Head Guard also soaks 1 damage off every attack on your Queen.
  31. 💥 Facing the martyrs: nearly every Veritas ant bursts when it dies — trade carelessly and the corpse takes your ant with it. An exploding ant killed by a spell or effect has no killer to catch, so its blast hits your Queen instead — unless the death is silenced (your Goo Burst does exactly that). And beware Detonate! — Veritas can blow up its own weakest ant on purpose to cash in the burst.
  32. 🕸️ Silk Weavers: Silk Spinner and Leaf Binder ask for a tap — play the ant, then tap the nestmate that gets the gift (+1 Health for good, or Guard until end of turn). A living Weaver Worker blunts every attack on your other ants by 1, a living Bridge Builder lets fresh ants attack at once, and Nest Stitch / Canopy Rally bonuses fade when your turn ends.
  33. 🍯 Living Reservoirs: living repletes raise your Food cap — and when one falls, its stored Food pays out on the spot. Fell on Veritas's turn? The Food is banked on top of your next refill, never lost. Replete Sacrifice costs 1 Food: tap it, then tap one of your ants to drain it — Food equal to its Health, plus a card, and its death gifts still trigger.
  34. 🍄 Zombie Ants — Infection: an infected ant wears a green 🍄 INFECTED badge. At the start of its owner's turn it attacks its own Queen for its Attack damage, then dies — and when any infected ant dies, its spores infect one random enemy ant, so the chain keeps moving one ant at a time. Infected ants fight and can be killed normally until then. Spore Infection and Spore Burst need a tap: play the spell, then tap the enemy ant. Death Grip forces the bite right now — the target hits its own Queen at once, then dies.

Colony glossary

Support cards — coming later. New card types that help your colony are planned, but they are not in the game yet.

⚖️ Canopy balance pass

Your list, kept almost card-for-card — three small tunings so it sits level with the other two decks: the Phragmotic Major's death burst is 2 to all enemy ants (as you wrote it — strong, but it's a single copy), Kamikaze Worker's 3-damage burst auto-aims at the best target (a killable ant first, otherwise the Queen — no mid-combat tapping), and Nest Seal's Guard lasts through Veritas's turn, expiring when your next turn starts — otherwise a one-turn Guard would vanish before it could ever block. Goo Burst's kill is silenced: no death effects, exactly the sticky trap you described.

💥 Veritas's new colony — the martyrs, balanced

Veritas picked the Exploding Ants (Colobopsis explodens) — a full 20-card deck built on autothysis, tuned to sit level with the other three decks. The bodies are deliberately ordinary (a 2/2 for 2, a 1/5 Guard for 3 — the same statlines the other decks pay), because the real cost is hidden: every death pays out a burst. That power is capped three ways — bursts mostly hit the killer, not the Queen, so a player who trades with big healthy ants shrugs them off; the deck has almost no direct Queen burn (no Raid! — its pressure has to walk in and die for it); and silencing a death (Goo Burst) or killing from behind a Guard denies the payout entirely. Its one trick the other decks don't have is Detonate! — spending a card and an ant to fire a burst on Veritas's own terms, strongest exactly when the board is already losing. The Army Ant deck stays in the lists below as the benchmark it was balanced against.

⚖️ First-turn balance

Going first is an advantage — you set the tempo, play the first ant, and threaten first. So the second player gets compensated, the way most card games do it: Veritas starts with 5 cards to your 4, and gets +1 Food on its first turn only (its food cap itself doesn't change — it's a one-turn bonus, logged when it's spent). Your first move still matters; it just isn't free anymore.

🕸️🍯 Two new colonies join the offline war

Silk Weavers (midrange control) win by building a line that won't die: permanent Health stitches from Spinners and the Major, a silk shield that blunts every attack, temporary Guards bound from leaves, and Bridge Builders whose living chains turn the whole colony hasty. Living Reservoirs (economy/tempo) win the Food war instead: repletes lift your Food cap while they hang in the nest and pay out when they fall — even mid-enemy-turn, banked for your next refill — and Replete Sacrifice turns any ant into Food equal to its Health plus a card, for just 1 Food. Both decks are built on the same benchmark as the rest: ordinary statlines for their cost, with the power living in the effects.

🍄 The seventh colony — Zombie Ants

Built around the real Ophiocordyceps fungus, which drives an ant's muscles while its brain stays a passenger, locks its jaws onto a leaf in a death grip, and rains spores onto the colony below. This deck copies the life cycle: infect one ant, and at the start of its owner's turn it bites its own Queen, dies, and the spores jump to one random enemy ant — one ant at a time, for as long as there are ants to catch it. The bodies are deliberately plain (a 2/2 for 2, a 3/3 for 3 — the same statlines every deck pays), because the damage was never meant to come from your side of the board: it comes from theirs. Its counters are honest ones — kill an infected ant on your own terms and the chain still jumps, but a thin enemy board starves the fungus of hosts, a 0-Attack host bites its own Queen for nothing.

⚡ The eighth colony — Trap-Jaw Ants

Built around the real Odontomachus snap — mandibles that shut at up to 140 mph, the fastest movement of any animal on Earth. This deck copies the trick as First-Strike ⚡: a snapping ant deals its damage first, and if the snap kills, the enemy never hits back — so small ants trade up and survive. The bodies are deliberately modest (nothing above 5 Attack, one 5-cost card) because the snap itself is the power, and the colony action (Snap, 1 damage for 1 Food) and ultimate (The Perfect Snap, 2 damage to the whole enemy line — or the Queen, if the line is empty) are the same idea at colony scale.
